0.long_answer: Granulocyte colony-stimulating factor (G-CSF) is a cytokine that plays a critical role in stimulating the bone marrow to produce and mature blood cells, particularly neutrophils. It is used as supportive therapy in conditions like Fanconi anemia, where bone marrow failure leads to deficiencies in blood cells. By promoting hematopoiesis, G-CSF helps to alleviate some of the hematologic complications associated with the disease.
